name: Edo polychrome nishiki-e printing
description: Edo printmakers used multiple registered woodblocks to produce full-colour single-sheet images, initially including commissioned calendars.

impact.note: Registered multi-block colour on existing woodblock printing; one society's print market, with the full-colour ukiyo-e line and its foreign influence following.

date.basis: The Met dates the first polychrome Edo calendars to 1765.

events.statement: Edo printmakers produced multicolour nishiki-e calendars commissioned by wealthy patrons.
events.scope: Early commissioned calendars, not the origin of all colour printing.

evidence.supports: Edo printmakers produced multicolour nishiki-e calendars commissioned by wealthy patrons.
The museum identifies a wealthy patron group commissioning the calendars.
The museum describes printmakers and multi-block printing.

earliest_record.rationale: Date and scope follow the cited event; this is the earliest episode established in this research, not a claim of world priority.

caveats: The 1765 calendars are a specific Edo development, not an invention date for woodblock printing or colour printing worldwide. The museum summarizes collaborative roles generally; it does not identify every participant in the first commissions.

research.note: Independent second reader checked the cited historical episodes, dates and actor roles against the stated source passages, subject to the caveats; other facets are not blanket reviewed.
